evidence: CVE Program record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2025-49179 is state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn) and describes RecordSanityCheckRegisterClients failing to check integer overflow when computing request length, CWE-190. Red Hat https://access.redhat.com/hydra/rest/securitydata/cve/CVE-2025-49179.json independently records the same CWE-190 mechanism and states the overflow can cause out-of-bounds read/write, crash, leak, or data corruption. First-party X.Org advisory https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2025-June/003608.html item 5 (CVE-2025-49179) matches that description and points at fix 2bde9ca49a8fd9a1e6697d5e7ef837870d66f5d4. GHSA-q547-25x8-mx66 is not withdrawn.

In d55c54cecb5e83eaa2d56bed5cc4461f9ba318c2:record/record.c (parent of the published fix), ProcRecordRegisterClients and ProcRecordCreateContext only require REQUEST_AT_LEAST_SIZE of the request header, then RecordRegisterClients calls RecordSanityCheckRegisterClients. That sanity check compares payload length ((client->req_len << 2) - SIZEOF(xRecordRegisterClientsReq)) to 4 * stuff->nClients + SIZEOF(xRecordRange) * stuff->nRanges with no prior bound on the attacker-controlled 32-bit nClients/nRanges fields (swapl on those fields in SwapCreateRegister).

If that arithmetic wraps, a short request can satisfy the equality. The same function then sets pRange = (xRecordRange *)(((XID *)&stuff[1]) + stuff->nClients) and loops i < stuff->nRanges, reading xRecordRange fields. RecordRegisterClients later re-derives pRanges the same way and passes them to RecordConvertRangesToIntervals, and also computes maxSets = RI_PREDEFSETS + 2 * stuff->nRanges. Source is the client RegisterClients/CreateContext counts; sink is out-of-request-buffer range reads plus subsequent interval conversion/allocation.

findings: CVE-2025-49179 / GHSA-q547-25x8-mx66 is a real, published CWE-190 integer overflow in RecordSanityCheckRegisterClients that lets attacker-controlled nClients/nRanges bypass the RECORD RegisterClients/CreateContext length check and then walk xRecordRange data out of the request buffer.

The smallest surviving public Git object that first writes those vulnerable lines in gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/xserver is ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (blob bcc019f27fec9e629ee00b0ab680506eb1866fd4); parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 has no record.c path and no finer in-repo member exists.

Direct fix is 2bde9ca49a8fd9a1e6697d5e7ef837870d66f5d4, shipped as cherry-picks 9d205323894af62b9726fcbaeb5fc69b3c9f61ba (xwayland-24.1.7 = 2c5e87e3dfecbd60bcad5b74cad2cdcf0a992b57) and 8592cab6820f77c209c2ea9a7b94e0d4d1ac848c (xorg-server-21.1.17 = 97f79ca01b6182e0ee987748fcdcbe276c84e0c9). Adjacent tags xwayland-24.1.6 and xorg-server-21.1.16 still carry the unbounded expression.

BIC-local attribution is named human Kaleb Keithley in 2003 with no AI/bot/generator marker, so the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI. FALSE_POSITIVE does not apply because CVE.org remains PUBLISHED and the source-to-sink is present in tree.
